According to the Turin Canon, this Hyksos ruler of Lower Egypt reigned forty years in the 16th century BC, outliving his southern rival Kamose but not Ahmose I. Who was he?
Apepi (Greek Apophis) was a Hyksos ruler of Lower Egypt during the Fifteenth Dynasty and the late Second Intermediate Period.

Fought in 1917 along the Isonzo front, this WWI clash saw Austro-Hungarian and German forces smash the Italian line using poison gas and newly developed stormtrooper infiltration tactics — which engagement was it?
Battle of Caporetto (also known as the Twelfth Battle of the Isonzo, the Battle of Kobarid or the Battle of Karfreit) took place on the Isonzo front of World War I.

Born a commoner in southern France and rising to Marshal of France under Napoleon, this monarch became king of Sweden and Norway in 1818 as the founder of a still-reigning royal dynasty — who was he?
Charles XIV John (26 January 1763 - 8 March 1844) was King of Sweden and Norway from 1818 until his death in 1844 and the first monarch of the Bernadotte dynasty.
This Indian National Congress politician became the 18th Chief Minister of the state of Karnataka in June 2026, after previously serving as its Deputy Chief Minister — who is he?

The 47th U.S. president, this businessman transformed his family's real estate company before launching numerous ventures and filing six business bankruptcies — who is he?
Donald Trump (born June 14, 1946) is an American politician, media personality, and businessman who is the 47th president of the United States.
This German author, soldier, and entomologist became famous for his World War I memoir Storm of Steel, writing more than 40 books over his long life — who is he?
Ernst Jünger (29 March 1895 - 17 February 1998) was a German author, soldier, philosopher, and entomologist who became publicly known for his World War I memoir Storm of Steel.
He began on the Catholic nationalist right and served under Vichy before moving left to become the first left-wing president of France's Fifth Republic — and its longest-serving. Who was he?
François Mitterrand (26 October 1916 - 8 January 1996) was President of France from 1981 to 1995.
Forced to abdicate in 1907 after 43 years on the throne, this monarch began as the 26th king of Joseon and became the first emperor of the Korean Empire — who is he?
Gojong of Korea (8 September 1852 - 21 January 1919), personal name Yi Jaehwang, later changed to Yi Hui, also known as the Gwangmu Emperor, was the penultimate Korean monarch.

This Sunni Islamist paramilitary group, born from a January 2017 merger of several Syrian rebel factions, spearheaded the offensive that ended over 13 years of civil war in December 2024 — which group?
Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) was a Sunni Islamist political organisation and paramilitary group involved in the Syrian civil war.
Founded in 1818 by a French-born Napoleonic marshal adopted as heir by Sweden's childless king, this royal dynasty still occupies the Swedish throne today — which dynasty?
House of Bernadotte is the royal family of Sweden, founded there in 1818 by King Charles XIV John.
This German-born businessman co-owned Macy's department store with his brother and briefly served in the U.S. House representing New York — who was he?
Isidor Straus (February 6, 1845 - April 15, 1912) was an American politician and businessman, who was a co-owner of Macy's department store with his brother Nathan.
A Labour Party economist who twice served as Norway's prime minister, he then led NATO as its secretary general from 2014 to 2024 — which politician is this?
Jens Stoltenberg (born 16 March 1959) is a Norwegian politician who has served as the minister of finance since 2025, a position he previously held from 1996 to 1997.
This East Timorese leader was the exiled voice of his country's resistance during Indonesian occupation and shared the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize before becoming president — who is he?

José Ramos-Horta (Portuguese; born 26 December 1949) is an East Timorese politician who has been the seventh president of Timor-Leste since 2022, having previously been the fourth president from 2007 to 2012.

The youngest Nobel laureate in history, she won the 2014 Peace Prize at 17 for championing girls' education in Pakistan's Swat district — who is she?
Malala Yousafzai (born 12 July 1997) is a Pakistani female education activist, and producer of film and television.
Founded around 320 BCE with its power base in Magadha, this Iron Age South Asian realm is chiefly documented through the later Edicts of a ruler named Ashoka — which empire?
Maurya Empire was a geographically extensive Iron Age historical power in South Asia with its power base in Magadha.
Known from the Mesha Stele, which describes its victory over the son of Israel's King Omri, this ancient Levantine kingdom's capital was Dibon, in what is now southern Jordan. Name the kingdom?
Moab was an ancient Levantine kingdom whose territory is today located in southern Jordan.

This Turkish politician served as his country's 23rd prime minister in 1996-97 before being pressured by the military to resign, and was later banned from politics for violating the constitution's secularism clause — who is he?
Necmettin Erbakan (29 October 1926 - 27 February 2011) was a Turkish politician and political theorist who served as the 23rd prime minister of Turkey from 1996 to 1997.
Meaning roughly 'salutations to the auspicious one,' this five-syllable Hindu mantra is the most important in Shaivism and is dedicated to Lord Shiva — what is it?
Om Namah Shivaya is one of the most popular Hindu mantras and the most important mantra in Shaivism.
This Czech politician and retired army general has served as his country's president since March 2023, after chairing NATO's Military Committee from 2015 to 2018 — who is he?
Petr Pavel (born 1 November 1961) is a Czech politician and retired army general, currently serving as the fourth president of the Czech Republic, in office since March 2023.
Trained as a psychiatrist, this Bosnian Serb leader was a fugitive for over a decade before being convicted of genocide by the ICTY — who is he?
Radovan Karadžić (Serbian; born 19 June 1945) is a Bosnian Serb former politician who served as the president of Republika Srpska during the Bosnian War.

Roberto Vannacci (born 20 October 1968) is a far-right politician and a retired Italian Army general.

Solomon was a king of ancient Israel. The successor of his father David, he is described as the penultimate ruler of all Twelve Tribes of Israel under a united Israel and Judah.
The second-longest-serving non-royal head of state in the world today, this dictator has ruled Equatorial Guinea since 1979, after ousting his own uncle in a military coup. Who is he?
Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo (born 5 June 1942) is an Equatoguinean politician, former military officer, and dictator who has served as the second president of Equatorial Guinea since 1979.

Born in the Ukrainian SSR and later Governor of Saint Petersburg from 2003 to 2011, this Russian politician has chaired the Federation Council since 2011 after earlier serving as ambassador to Malta and Greece — who is she?
Valentina Matviyenko (ne Tyutina; born 7 April 1949) is a Russian politician and former diplomat serving as a Senator from Saint Petersburg and the Chairwoman of the Federation Council since 2011.

Balenciaga: France-based Spanish luxury fashion house.

Benjamin Netanyahu: Prime Minister of Israel (1996–1999; 2009–2021; 2022–present)

Great Smog of London: 1952 air pollution event. It lasted from Friday, 5 December to Tuesday, 9 December 1952, then dispersed quickly when the weather changed.

Henry VIII: King of England from 1509 to 1547.

House of Plantagenet: Angevin royal dynasty that ruled England in the Middle Ages.

Imjin War: 1592–1598 Japanese invasions of Korea. The conflict ended in 1598 with the withdrawal of Japanese forces from the Korean Peninsula after a military stalemate in Korea's southern provinces.

JB Pritzker: Governor of Illinois since 2019.

Charles I of Spain awarded this navigator a coat of arms reading "Primus circumdedisti me" — "You were the first to circumnavigate me" — after he completed the first voyage around the Earth aboard the Victoria. Who was he?
Juan Sebastián Elcano: Spanish seafarer and circumnavigator.

Kemalism: Founding ideology of the Republic of Türkiye.

Leonidas I: King of Sparta from c. 489 BC to 480 BC.

Louis XIV: King of France from 1643 to 1715.

Malcolm III of Scotland: King of Alba from 1058 to 1093. Throughout his reign, Malcolm III led at least five invasions into English territory.

Olaf Scholz: Chancellor of Germany from 2021 to 2025. Olaf Scholz (born 14 June 1958) is a German politician who served as the chancellor of Germany from 2021 to 2025.

Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha: Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire from 1523 to 1536. Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha (c. 1495 – 15 March 1536), was the first grand vizier of the Ottoman Empire appointed by Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent.

Psalms: Book of sacred songs in the Hebrew Bible.

Vasili III of Russia: Grand Prince of Moscow from 1505 to 1533.

Georg Cantor is a mathematician. Cantor's method of proof of this theorem implies the existence of an infinity of infinities.
What is the atomic number of Radon?
Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
What is the atomic number of Gallium?
Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.
In what year did Alexander Hamilton die?
Alexander Hamilton: Born out of wedlock in Charlestown on the Caribbean island of Nevis, Hamilton was orphaned as a child and taken in by a prosperous merchant.
In what year was Uncertainty principle discovered?

Who is credited with discovering Musca?
Musca: Petrus Plancius. Musca (Latin for 'the fly') is a small constellation in the deep southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Testosterone?

Who is credited with discovering Rubidium?

Belonging to the birch family and numbering about 35 species, these monoecious trees and shrubs are found across the north temperate zone, with a few extending into Central America and the Andes — name this genus of tree?
Alder are trees of the genus Alnus in the birch family Betulaceae.
This unit of length equals one ten-billionth of a meter, or 100 picometres, and is named after a 19th-century Swedish physicist — what is it?
Angstrom (ONG-) is a unit of length equal to 1010 m; that is, one ten-billionth of a metre, a hundred-millionth of a centimetre, 0.1 nanometre, or 100 picometres.
This American physicist won a share of the 1927 Nobel Prize for an effect, now bearing his name, that demonstrated light's particle nature — who was he?
Arthur Compton (September 10, 1892 - March 15, 1962) was an American physicist who shared the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics with C. T. R. Wilson.
The first production aircraft of its type, this American military transport combines vertical takeoff and landing with long-range cruise performance—what is it?
Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey is an American multi-use, tiltrotor military transport and cargo aircraft with both vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) and short takeoff and landing (STOL) capabilities.
This leafy vegetable forms no head, just green blades atop pale bulbous stalks, with a flavor often compared to a mix of spinach and water chestnut — what vegetable is it?

Bok choy (American English, Canadian English, and Australian English), pak choi (British English, South African English, and Caribbean English) or pok choi is a type of Chinese cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp.
This soft, silvery-white metal shares group 12 of the periodic table with zinc and mercury, resembling zinc in its chemistry and mercury in its low melting point — what element, symbol Cd, is it?
Cadmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cd and atomic number 48.
Named for the whisker-like barbels many species sport, these scaleless ray-finned fish include some of the largest freshwater giants in Southeast Asia and Eurasia — name this diverse group of fish?
Catfish are a diverse group of ray-finned fish of the order Siluriformes (historically Nematognathi).
A notorious household nuisance pest that feeds on sleeping humans, this insect has never been shown to actually transmit disease to people — what is it?
Cimex lectularius is a species of Cimicidae.
Entering service with Strategic Air Command in 1960, this four-engine, delta-wing supersonic bomber was the first in the world capable of Mach 2 — name the aircraft?

Convair B-58 Hustler is a supersonic strategic bomber, the first capable of Mach 2 flight. To achieve the high speeds desired, Convair chose a delta wing design used by contemporary interceptors such as the Convair F-102.
A staunch defender of Georg Cantor's set theory, this mathematician co-founded proof theory and became one of the most influential figures in his field — who is he?
David Hilbert (23 January 1862 - 14 February 1943) was a German mathematician and philosopher of mathematics and one of the most influential mathematicians of all time.
This waterfowl belongs to the same family as swans and geese, but is generally smaller and shorter-necked — and despite the shared family, swans and geese don't count as one. What is it?
Duck is the common name for numerous species of waterfowl in the family Anatidae.

It's the creation of economic value by spotting and commercializing opportunities — a venture that demands serious initiative and shoulders real risk. What is this process, named from a French word for the risk-taker who runs it?

Entrepreneurship is the creation or extraction of economic value by identifying and commercializing opportunities to deliver products or services, a process that typically requires considerable initiation and bears risk.
A legume plant from the family Fabaceae, its leaves and seeds have been common in dishes from the Indian subcontinent since ancient times — what is it?
Fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum) is an annual plant in the family Fabaceae, with leaves consisting of three small obovate to oblong leaflets.
Son of a wealthy Greek architect, this 2nd-century physician and philosopher's writings shaped anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, and neurology for centuries after his death — who is he?
This applied art and academic discipline uses text and images to craft visual communications aimed at specific audiences and objectives — what field is it?
Graphic design is a profession, academic discipline and applied art that involves creating visual communications intended to transmit specific messages to social groups, with specific objectives.
Credited with putting middle-class Americans behind the wheel, this industrialist lent his surname to the very philosophy of assembly-line manufacturing. Who is he?
Henry Ford (July 30, 1863 - April 7, 1947) was an American industrialist and business magnate.
This endocrine condition floods the body with thyroid hormone, causing a racing heart, heat intolerance, tremor, and weight loss — and a rare 'storm' can be deadly; what is it?
Hyperthyroidism is a endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland produces excessive amounts of thyroid hormones.

A colorless, flammable organic compound with a pungent odor, this liquid is miscible in water, ethanol, and chloroform, and is widely used as a solvent and disinfectant. It's commonly abbreviated as IPA—what is it?
Isopropyl alcohol (IUPAC name propan-2-ol and also called isopropanol or 2-propanol, commonly abbreviated as IPA) is a colorless, flammable, organic compound with a pungent odor.

An Alberta-raised classical liberal who earned his PhD in clinical psychology at McGill and taught at Harvard before the University of Toronto, this commentator drew huge attention in the late 2010s — who is he?
Jordan Peterson (born 12 June 1962) is a Canadian psychologist, author, and media commentator.
This American economist served as U.S. Treasury Secretary, later led the National Economic Council, and was the 27th president of Harvard before resigning a professorship there in 2026 — who is he?
Larry Summers (born November 30, 1954) is an American economist.
Known mainly from fossils in Peru's Pisco Formation, this Miocene-era macroraptorial sperm whale takes its name from a biblical sea monster — what is it called?
Livyatan is an extinct genus of highly predatory macroraptorial sperm whale, containing one known species: L. melvillei.
Its Spanish name translates to 'little apple of death' — this tropical tree's apple-like fruit and toxic milky sap make it one of the most poisonous trees on Earth — which tree?
Manchineel (Hippomane mancinella), also known as the tree of death, is a species of flowering plant in the spurge family (Euphorbiaceae).

Patented in 1922 and used to relieve pain, fever, and spasms, this drug's sale is restricted in some countries due to a rare but serious blood-cell side effect discovered in the 1970s — what drug is it?
Metamizole is a painkiller, spasm reliever, and fever reliever drug.
First synthesized in 2003 by Russian and American scientists at Dubna, this synthetic element — atomic number 115 — was named in 2016 for the oblast around its birthplace — what is it?
Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
Found in tiny native amounts in Earth's crust but riding inside iron meteorites that never met oxygen, this hard, ductile metal shares its name with a small coin — which element is it?
Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
These red-haired great apes once roamed all of Southeast Asia but now cling to just Borneo and Sumatra — and in 2017 scientists confirmed a brand-new third species among them. Which animal is it?
Orangutan are great apes native to the rainforests of Indonesia and Malaysia.
Which American biologist became famous for the controversial 1968 book 'The Population Bomb' and its dire warnings about population growth, famine, and resource depletion?

Paul R. Ehrlich (May 29, 1932 - March 13, 2026) was an American biologist, author, and environmentalist known for his predictions and warnings about the consequences of population growth, including famine and resource depletion.

This class of lipid molecules has a water-loving 'head' built around a phosphate group and two water-fearing fatty-acid 'tails' — and forms an essential building block of neuronal membranes in the brain. Name the class of molecule?

Phospholipid are a class of lipids whose molecule has a hydrophilic "head" containing a phosphate group and two hydrophobic "tails" derived from fatty acids, joined by an alcohol residue (usually a glycerol molecule).
Known as little hogweed or pursley, every part of this succulent plant can be eaten raw or cooked — what plant is it?
Portulaca oleracea (common purslane, also known as little hogweed, or pursley) is a succulent plant in the family Portulacaceae.
This set of three positive whole numbers, like (3, 4, 5), satisfies a squared plus b squared equals c squared and forms the side lengths of a right triangle — what is it called?
Pythagorean triple consists of three positive integers a, b, and c, such that a2 + b2 = c2.
As chairman of the now-defunct Purdue Pharma, he oversaw the launch of OxyContin — a tenure dramatized in Hulu's Dopesick and Netflix's Painkiller; who is he?
Richard Sackler (born March 10, 1945) is an American businessman, pharmaceutical entrepreneur and physician who was the chairman and president of Purdue Pharma, a now-defunct pharmaceutical company.

Often striking suddenly after heavy lifting and described as a shooting pain down one leg, about 90% of cases trace to a spinal disc herniation pressing on a nerve root — what's this condition called?
Sciatica is pain going down the leg from the lower back.
This Irish mathematician and physicist held Cambridge's Lucasian chair for a record 54 years and lent his name to a theorem in vector calculus and to equations of fluid motion — who was he?
Sir George Stokes, 1st Baronet (stohks; 13 August 1819 - 1 February 1903), was an Irish mathematician and physicist.
This round, gram-positive germ lives harmlessly on most people's skin and noses, but turn opportunistic and it triggers abscesses, sinus infections, and food poisoning. What is it?

Staphylococcus aureus is a gram-positive spherically shaped bacterium, a member of the Bacillota, and is a usual member of the microbiota of the body, frequently found in the upper respiratory tract and on the skin.
These large, often hairy spiders of the family Theraphosidae number over a thousand species, and New World pet varieties can flick irritating 'urticating hairs' at threats. What creatures are they?
Tarantula are a group of large and often hairy spiders of the family Theraphosidae.

Affecting roughly 10 to 15 percent of people, this condition causes a person to hear ringing or other sounds with no external source, and its name comes from the Latin word for 'to ring' — what is it?
Tinnitus is a condition when a person hears a ringing sound or a different variety of sounds when no corresponding external sound is present and that other people cannot hear.
This medical specialty, whose name derives from the Greek word for urine, covers surgical and medical treatment of the urinary tract and the male reproductive organs — name this field?

Urology (from Greek ouron "urine" and - -logia "study of"), also known as genitourinary surgery, is the branch of medicine that focuses on surgical and medical diseases of the urinary system and the male reproductive organs.
The first-ever recipient of the Nobel Prize in Physics, this German scientist discovered a form of electromagnetic radiation named after him in some languages — who was he?

Wilhelm Röntgen (27 March 1845 - 10 February 1923) was a German experimental physicist who produced and detected electromagnetic radiation in a wavelength range known as X-rays (known as Rntgen rays in many languages).

This symptom can stem from something as mild as gastroenteritis or as serious as a ruptured aortic aneurysm or ectopic pregnancy, yet its exact cause goes unexplained in about a third of cases — what symptom is this?
Native to China and Taiwan, this fast-growing deciduous tree can reach 15 meters in 25 years and has become notorious in North America as a host plant for the invasive spotted lanternfly. What is it?
Ailanthus altissima: Deciduous tree in the quassia family.
This military pilot became his country's first astronaut when he flew to the International Space Station aboard a 2024 mission — who is he?
Alper Gezeravcı: Turkish fighter pilot and astronaut (born 1979)

Coming on slowly it brings vague fatigue and breathlessness; arriving suddenly it can cause confusion and fainting — and only when it's severe does a person look pale — which blood disorder reduces the blood's oxygen-carrying ability?
Anemia: Reduced ability of blood to carry oxygen.
This genus of orb-weaving spiders, encompassing the European garden spider and the barn spider among its 500-plus species, was named by an 18th-century Swedish naturalist in 1757 — which genus?
Araneus: Genus of spiders. The genus was erected by Carl Alexander Clerck in 1757.

Related to the tufted and horned members of its family found in the Pacific, this seabird breeds from Iceland to Newfoundland and dives underwater to catch zooplankton, small fish and crabs — which auk is this?
Atlantic puffin: Species of seabird. The Atlantic puffin (Fratercula arctica), also known as the common puffin, is a species of seabird in the auk family.
Second only to the capybara among living rodents and able to top 50 kg, this animal sports chisel-like incisors, webbed back feet, and a flat, scaly tail — what is it?
This class of aquatic molluscs — including clams, oysters, mussels, and scallops — has no head and encloses its soft body in a hinged pair of shells called valves — which class?
Bivalvia: Class of molluscs. The shell of a bivalve is composed of calcium carbonate, and consists of two, usually similar, parts called valves.
Rooted in prehistoric herbalism for identifying edible and medicinal species, this branch of biology studies roughly 410,000 species of land plants — what field of study?
Named from the Greek word for butter, this oily, foul-smelling compound with the formula CH3CH2CH2COOH is a key component of the mammalian gut. What is it?
Butyric acid: Chemical compound (CH3CH2CH2COOH). It is an oily, colorless liquid with an unpleasant odor.
Discovered by a Swiss chemist in 1953 and sold as Tegretol, this anticonvulsant treats epilepsy and neuropathic pain and sits on the WHO's list of essential medicines. Which drug is it?
Carbamazepine: Anticonvulsant medication. Carbamazepine, sold under the brand name Tegretol among others, is an anticonvulsant medication used in the treatment of epilepsy and neuropathic pain.
Every one of these segmented arthropods is venomous, delivering its sting through pincer-like 'legs' rather than fangs — and despite its name, none has exactly 100 of those legs — what is it?
Centipede: Many-legged arthropods with elongated bodies.
Packed with chlorophyll, this plant-cell organelle captures sunlight, splits water to release oxygen, and feeds sugar-making in the Calvin cycle — what is it called?
Chloroplast: Plant organelle that conducts photosynthesis.
A tropane alkaloid drawn from the leaves of South American coca plants, it once served doctors as a local anesthetic with handy vasoconstricting properties — what is this stimulant?

Cocaine: Tropane alkaloid and stimulant drug. The leaves are processed into cocaine paste, a crude mixture of coca alkaloids, from which cocaine base is isolated and then converted to cocaine hydrochloride.
The first bomber capable of Mach 2 flight, this 1950s delta-winged bomber carried its nuclear payload in a combination bomb-and-fuel pod slung beneath the fuselage — which bomber?
Convair B-58 Hustler: Cold War-era American supersonic bomber.
Caused by prolonged exposure to excess cortisol, this condition produces abdominal weight gain with thin limbs, a rounded red face, and reddish stretch marks — which condition is it?
Cushing's syndrome: Symptoms from excessive exposure to glucocorticoids such as cortisol.
Working alongside longtime colleague Ken Thompson, this American computer scientist co-created the Unix operating system and the C programming language — who is he?
Dennis Ritchie: American computer scientist known for Unix (1941–2011)
Nicknamed 'Spad' after a World War I fighter, this piston-engine attack plane flew from 1946 into the 1980s, an anachronism deep into the Jet Age — which aircraft?
Douglas A-1 Skyraider: American single engine attack aircraft.
Linked with orgasm and involving involuntary pelvic-floor contractions, this male bodily process can even happen during sleep as a so-called 'wet dream' — what is it?
Ejaculation: Semen discharge from the male reproductive tract.
This 1939 Nobel Physics laureate invented the cyclotron and went on to found two national laboratories that carry his surname today — who was he?

Scientifically known as Chloris chloris, this small finch is widespread across Europe, North Africa, and Southwest Asia, and has also been introduced to Australia, New Zealand, Uruguay, and Argentina — what bird is this?
European greenfinch: Species of bird. The European greenfinch or simply the greenfinch (Chloris chloris) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.
Historically used in the 18th century to track down escaped slaves, this large Brazilian dog breed of mastiff type now also serves as a guard dog and companion — which breed?
Fila Brasileiro: Brazilian breed of dog. The Fila Brasileiro (Portuguese pronunciation: [ˈfilɐ bɾaziˈlejɾu]) is a Brazilian breed of large working dog of mastiff type.

Coated in cornmeal and pan-cooked while still unripe, this dish was originally a Northeastern and Midwestern staple before a hit movie rebranded it as quintessentially Southern comfort food — what is it?
Fried green tomatoes: American dish. Fried green tomatoes is a culinary dish usually found in the United States, made from unripe (green) tomatoes coated with cornmeal and fried.

Working at Tuskegee Institute, this agricultural scientist urged cotton farmers to plant peanuts and sweet potatoes instead, publishing dozens of practical bulletins to fight soil depletion. Who is he?
George Washington Carver: American botanist and inventor (1864–1943)

This German engineer invented the high-speed petroleum engine, working alongside his lifelong partner Wilhelm Maybach to build small, fast motors they hoped to mount on any kind of vehicle. Who was he?
Gottlieb Daimler: German engineer, industrialist and automotive pioneer (1834–1900)
Often translated as 'Jewish law' but literally meaning 'the way of walking,' this body of religious rules draws on the Torah, the Talmud, and codes like the Shulchan Aruch — what is it called?
Halakha: Jewish rabbinical law. Halakha is often translated as "Jewish law", although a more literal translation might be "the way one proceeds" or "the way of walking".
With over 800 species lugging borrowed snail shells to shield their soft, non-calcified abdomens, this crustacean is essentially homeless without a hand-me-down home. What is it?
Stretching about a meter from crown to tail-tip, this deep-blue South American parrot is the largest of its kind and can be mistaken for a smaller relative — which vulnerable parrot?
The world's largest jet airliner when it first flew in 1963, this Soviet quad-engine jetliner entered Aeroflot service with a Moscow-to-Montreal flight in 1967. What aircraft?
Ilyushin Il-62: Soviet long-range narrow-body four-engined jet airliner.
The biggest cat in the Americas, it has a bite so powerful it can crack a turtle's shell or punch straight through a skull between the ears — which animal?
Jaguar: Large cat native to the Americas.
This New Zealand-American sexologist at Johns Hopkins coined the very phrases 'gender role' and 'sexual orientation' — which controversial researcher is it?
John Money: New Zealand psychologist and sexologist (1921–2006)
Nicknamed the 'honey bear' though unrelated to actual bears, this nocturnal rainforest mammal is the only member of its genus and a cousin of raccoons and coatis — which arboreal creature?
A hybrid of the citron and the bitter orange, this small evergreen tree may have first appeared in northeastern India, and its fruit's juice is about 5–6% citric acid — what is it?
Also called pseudocoma, this condition leaves a fully conscious patient paralyzed except for blinking and vertical eye movement, coined by two neurologists in 1966 — what is it called?
Locked-in syndrome: Condition in which a patient is aware but completely paralysed.
Nicknamed for a Native American tribe, this mulberry-family tree produces a bumpy, orange-like fruit that oozes sticky white latex and is rarely eaten by animals — what's its scientific name?
Maclura pomifera: Plant species in the fig family.
In 2014 this Stanford mathematician became the first woman and first Iranian to win the Fields Medal, honored for her work on the geometry of Riemann surfaces — who was she?
Aristotle called it the 'first philosophy' — the branch that probes existence itself, what all things have in common, and how reality is divided into categories of being. Which field is it?
This Israeli-American physician turned billionaire donor owns the Las Vegas Review-Journal and Dallas Mavericks, and was one of Donald Trump's largest financial backers — who is she?

Miriam Adelson: Israeli-American physician, billionaire, and conservative donor. Miriam Adelson (née Farbstein; born October 10, 1945) is an Israeli-American physician, businesswoman, philanthropist, and conservative political donor.
Serving as Turkey's minister overseeing environment and climate, who is set to preside over the 2026 UN Climate Change Conference, COP31?
A healthy kidney contains up to 1.5 million of these microscopic filtering units, each pairing a capillary tuft with a cup-shaped capsule — what is it called?
Nephron: Microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney.
Represented by symbols like '11' in the Hindu-Arabic system used worldwide, these mathematical objects serve to count, measure, and label — what are they called?
Number: Used to count, measure, and label. The most basic examples are the natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so forth.
Described as far back as the 300s BC by Hippocrates, this bone infection most often strikes the spine in adults and the long bones in children — which condition?
Osteomyelitis: Infection of the bones. It may be acute or chronic and can be classified as hematogenous or non-hematogenous.
Also known as trisomy 13, this chromosomal condition arises when cells carry extra genetic material from chromosome 13, causing widespread organ defects — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome: Chromosomal disorder in which there are three copies of chromosome 13.
This legume's raw seeds contain a toxic compound that must be boiled away before eating, though its unripe green pods are eaten as-is — which species is it?
Named from a Greek word meaning 'wanderers,' these large rounded bodies orbit a star or similar object — our solar system has eight, from Mercury to Neptune. What are they called?
Planet: Large, round non-stellar astronomical object.
Marked by high blood pressure and protein in the urine after 20 weeks of pregnancy, this disorder can progress to seizures if left untreated — what is it called?
Excess fluid pooling in the lungs' air sacs impairs oxygen exchange and can be triggered by either heart failure or a range of unrelated causes — what condition is this?
Pulmonary edema: Fluid accumulation in the tissue and air spaces of the lungs.
This bird of prey, related to eagles and buzzards, now breeds only in Europe but has wandered as far as Finland and the Gambia — what raptor is it?
Red kite: Species of bird. The red kite (Milvus milvus) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as eagles, buzzards, and harriers.
Defined by a single pair of ever-growing incisors in each jaw, this mammalian order makes up about 40 percent of all mammal species — which order?
Rodent: Order of mammals. The rodent fossil record dates back to the Paleocene of Asia.
Commonly known as elder, with its blossoms called elderflower and its fruit elderberry, this genus contains between 20 and 30 flowering plant species — which genus?
The sole living species in its genus, this coastal California evergreen is the tallest tree species on Earth, reaching over 116 meters and living 2,200 years or more. What is it?
Sequoia sempervirens: Species of tree. Sequoia sempervirens is the sole living species of the genus Sequoia in the cypress family Cupressaceae (formerly treated in Taxodiaceae).

Named in 1842 from Brazilian fossils and often called a saber-toothed tiger despite no close kinship to true tigers, this genus of prehistoric predator roamed the Americas until the early Holocene — which animal?
Smilodon: Extinct genus of saber-toothed cat.
It's the largest order of reptiles — lizards and snakes alike — set apart by horny scales they periodically shed and a hinged upper jaw that lets snakes gape around big prey. Which order?
Squamata: Order of reptiles. The now-extinct mosasaurs reached lengths over 14 m (46 ft).
A sphere of plasma heated to incandescence by nuclear fusion in its core, it radiates mostly visible light and infrared — plus about 10% as what?
The Sun is a massive sphere of hot plasma heated by nuclear fusion in its core, radiating energy mainly as visible light and infrared radiation, with about 10% at ultraviolet energies.
The earliest known example was the stone tool, and the later control of fire is even credited with helping grow the human brain and spark language — what broad field is being described?
Technology: Use of knowledge for practical goals.
Tucked behind the breastbone and in front of the heart, this two-lobed organ is where immature T cells mature, and it's most active before adolescence — which organ?
About 70% of people infected with this parasite-caused sexually transmitted infection show no symptoms at all, though it can raise the risk of contracting HIV — what condition is it?
Trichomoniasis: Medical condition. Trichomoniasis (trich) is an infectious disease caused by the parasite Trichomonas vaginalis.
Formed by the fusion of membrane vesicles, this shapeless organelle in plant and fungal cells is basically a water-filled storage sac that can even hold engulfed solids. What is it?
Vacuole: Membrane-bound organelle in cells containing fluid.
One of the oldest leaf vegetables eaten by humans, this aquatic member of the cabbage family shares its peppery bite with relatives like mustard, radish, and wasabi — what is it?
Watercress: Species of flowering plant in the cabbage family.
Making up only about 1% of described fungal species, this single-celled organism reproduces by budding or fission and is so tiny it usually measures just 3 to 4 micrometres across — what is it?
The symbol for argon is Ar. Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
